checks.label: Your listing category says you provide home care
checks.unavailableReason: Google shares only a broad type for care businesses ("Health"), not the category you chose, so we could not read it. Worth checking yourself: the primary category should be "Home care service" or "Home health care service", and it decides which searches you appear in.

checks.label: Your listing shows when you can be reached
checks.detail: Your listing has no hours on it.
checks.fix: Add hours — and if you answer the phone around the clock, say so.
steps: Open your Business Profile and set your office hours.
If someone always answers, set the hours to open 24 hours: families call in a crisis, and at 9pm a closed listing loses the call.

checks.label: Your listing has photos
checks.detail: Only 1 photo on your listing.
checks.fix: Get to ten or more photos of real caregivers and real staff.
steps: Photograph your office team and (with written permission) caregivers with clients.
Upload ten or more. Stock photography reads as stock photography and families discount it.
Add a few every quarter — a listing that never changes looks dormant.

Claim it if it does, create it if it does not.

checks.label: Your phone number is one tap away
checks.detail: Your number is on the page as text, but it is not a tap-to-call link.
checks.fix: Make the number a link so a phone dials it when tapped.
steps: Ask whoever maintains the site to wrap the number in a tel: link.
Keep it visible in the header on a phone, not only in the footer.

checks.label: Your site lists the towns you cover
checks.detail: We could not find anywhere on your site that names the towns you serve.
checks.fix: Add an "Areas we serve" page naming every town and zip code.
steps: Write down every city, county and zip code your caregivers actually travel to.
Put them on one page called "Areas we serve" and link it from the main menu.
You are a service-area business: this list is the single strongest local signal you own.

checks.label: Your page title says where you work
checks.detail: Your town is on the page but not in the title or main heading.
checks.fix: Put the town in the page title and the main heading.
steps: Change your homepage title to something like "Home Care in Uniontown, PA | Lindsay's Loving Home Care Agency, LLC".
Make the main heading say the same thing in plain words.

checks.label: Each kind of care you offer has its own page
checks.detail: You name 2 services but they mostly share one page.
checks.fix: Give each service its own page with its own heading.
steps: Make one page each for the services you really sell — personal care, companion care, dementia care, respite, 24-hour care.
On each, say who it is for, what a caregiver actually does, and what it costs per hour.
One page per service is one more search you can win; a single "Services" page wins one.

checks.label: Your site describes itself to search engines
checks.detail: We found no business markup on your site.
checks.fix: Add HomeHealthCareBusiness (or LocalBusiness) markup with your phone, hours and service area.
steps: Ask your web person for JSON-LD markup on the homepage.
Use type HomeHealthCareBusiness, and include name, telephone, url, openingHours and areaServed.
Test it in Google's Rich Results Test.

checks.label: A family can ask for care without phoning
checks.detail: There is a contact form.

checks.label: Your site works on a phone and is secure
checks.detail: Secure, and built to resize on a phone.

checks.label: Your site says your caregivers are vetted
checks.detail: We found nothing on your site about screening or licensing.
checks.fix: Say how caregivers are screened, and name your license.
steps: State that caregivers are background-checked, bonded and insured.
Add your state license number.
This is the first question every family asks about letting a stranger into a parent's home.

checks.label: Caregivers can find and apply for a job
checks.detail: You have a careers page at /career/.

checks.label: Your site says how families can pay
checks.detail: Your site says little about what care costs or how families pay for it.
checks.fix: Add a page on cost and payment options.
steps: Give an hourly range, even a wide one. Families who cannot find a price assume the worst and call someone else.
List what you accept: private pay, long-term care insurance, Medicaid waiver, VA benefits.
Say plainly that Medicare does not pay for non-medical home care — it is the most common misunderstanding you can clear up.

checks.label: Your star rating stands up
checks.detail: 3.4 stars on Google. Below four stars, families stop calling.
checks.fix: Get your Google rating back above four stars — nothing else on this list turns away as many families.
steps: Read the one- and two-star reviews for the pattern; there usually is one.
Fix the pattern, then reply to each review saying what changed.
Ask happy families for reviews steadily, not in one burst.

checks.label: You have enough reviews to be believed
checks.detail: Only 9 reviews on Google. A handful reads as a new agency, whatever your rating.
checks.fix: Build up to at least 25 Google reviews.
steps: Get your Google review link from your Business Profile.
Text it to the families you know are happy — a few each week.
Never buy reviews or offer anything for them; Google removes them and it is worse than having none.

checks.label: Reviews are still arriving
checks.detail: Your most recent review is 631 days old, which reads as an agency that stopped.
checks.fix: Get reviews arriving again, and keep them arriving.
steps: Ask your current families this month.
Then keep asking, one a week, indefinitely — freshness counts as much as the total.

checks.label: You have reviews somewhere besides Google
checks.detail: We found no Yelp reviews for you.
checks.fix: Claim your Yelp listing so reviews have somewhere else to land.
steps: Claim the listing at biz.yelp.com.
Fill in services, hours and service area.
Do not solicit Yelp reviews — Yelp filters solicited ones out. Claim it, keep it accurate, and let it sit.

checks.label: Your own site shows what families say
checks.detail: We found no testimonials on your website.
checks.fix: Put real quotes from families on the site, with first name and town.
steps: Ask three families for permission to quote them.
Put the quotes on the homepage and a testimonials page.
Include the town — "Susan, Virginia Beach" is a local signal as well as a reference.

modules.label: Whether AI can quote your site

checks.label: One plain sentence says what you are and where
checks.detail: You say it, but not at the top of the homepage where it gets lifted from.
checks.fix: Move the plain sentence to the top of the homepage.
steps: Write: "Lindsay's Loving Home Care Agency, LLC is a home care agency serving Uniontown and the surrounding area."
Put it in the first paragraph, as ordinary text.
It will read as almost too obvious. That is the point — it is the sentence an assistant repeats.

checks.label: Your headings answer the questions families ask
checks.detail: Only 1 heading on your site is written as a question.
checks.fix: Turn the questions you answer on the phone every day into headings.
steps: Write down the ten questions you actually get asked.
Make each one a heading, with a two-sentence answer under it.
"How much does home care cost in Uniontown?" is a heading. "Our Services" is not.

checks.label: Your questions are marked up for machines
checks.detail: We found no FAQ markup on your site.
checks.fix: Add FAQPage markup around your questions and answers.
steps: Ask your web person to add FAQPage JSON-LD to the FAQ page.
Test it in Google's Rich Results Test.

checks.label: Your headings pair a service with a town
checks.detail: No heading names both a service and your town.
checks.fix: Write headings that pair the two: "Dementia care in Uniontown".
steps: For each service page, make the heading "<service> in <town>".
Do it for the two or three towns that actually matter, not for fifty — a page per town with nothing new on it is a page nobody ranks.

checks.label: Your site says what an hour of care costs
checks.detail: Your site does not mention what care costs.
checks.fix: Give an hourly range. "Contact us for pricing" is not an answer an assistant can repeat.
steps: Add: "Home care in Uniontown typically costs $X to $Y an hour."
Explain what changes the number — hours per week, level of care, overnight.
This is the most-asked question of every AI assistant about home care, and the one most agency sites refuse to answer.

checks.label: Your pages have enough readable text
checks.detail: Your homepage carries about 348 words of text.

checks.label: Something on your site is recent and dated
checks.detail: There are recent dates but no article section we could find.
checks.fix: Publish something dated, a few times a year.
steps: Write one short piece a quarter answering a real question — "How to know when a parent needs help at home".
Show the date. A site with no dates on it looks abandoned to a machine deciding whether to trust it.
